qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Deeply embedded defense (Gotham/Maven/TITAN) and commercial ontology (Foundry/AIP) workflows create high switching barriers. Verified by 2023-2025 GAAP ROIC expanding from ~14% to >60%, net dollar retention >115%, and strong pricing power on contract expansions.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While defense clearances (Gotham/Maven) and ontology workflows create high switching costs, Palantir's commercial AI platform operates in Tier 3 enterprise software with high fade rates and fast-evolving competition from hyperscalers (Microsoft, AWS, Google) and data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake), capping structural runway at 10 years. Downstream governance (Class F 49.999999% founder voting lock) and extreme historical SBC dilution further violate Munger partnership standards.
qualitative.evidence: Palantir scaled rapidly following AIP introduction, with FY2024 revenue reaching $2.87B (+29% YoY) and FY2025 revenue hitting $4.48B (+56% YoY). GAAP profitability was achieved in FY2023 ($210M net income), expanding to $468M in FY2024 and $1.63B in FY2025 (36% net margin). Free cash flow reached $1.1B in FY2024 and $2.27B in FY2025 (51% FCF margin). Balance sheet is debt-free with $7.2B in cash, equivalents, and US Treasuries as of FY2025. ROIC expanded from negative in 2020-2022 to ~14% in 2023 and >60% in 2025. Despite these stellar recent financial results, the company fails the 15+ year Competitive Advantage Period (CAP) threshold under the Mauboussin persistence framework (Tier 3 enterprise software base rate persistence p=0.75-0.79, fade f=0.21-0.25). Enterprise software application platforms face rapid obsolescence and technological evolution over a 15-year horizon. Furthermore, Palantir exhibits egregious corporate governance flaws: co-founders Alex Karp, Peter Thiel, and Stephen Cohen maintain permanent ~50% voting control via Class F variable-voting shares regardless of economic share sales, entirely disenfranchising outside public shareholders.
